newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Hallenstein expects lower first half.
newsitem.headline: Hallenstein expects lower first half.

text.p: New Zealand retailer Hallenstein Glasson Ltd said on Tuesday that based on trading patterns up until the end of November its first half result would not match that of 1995/96.
Chairman Warren Bell told shareholders the company had faced a very difficult start to the new summer season.
Last year Hallenstein made a first half net profit of NZ$6.5 million.

Bell said consumer spending as Christmas approached continued to be adversely affected by the slowing domestic economy and political uncertainty surrounding the October general election. Negotiations have so far failed to produce a coalition government.
No sales lift has been experienced from tax cuts which took effect on July 1.
Total sales for the first four months to November 30 were approximately 0.5 percent behind the same period last year.
However, this figure included seven new store openings which occurred during October 1996.
Adjusting to a store "like for like" basis, this equated to existing stores trading approximately six percent below the same period last year.
"Based on trading patterns to date, and sales achieved to November 30, your board consider last year's first half results will not be able to be attained this year," Bell said.
He added that the company was financially strong and very well placed to benefit from any upturn in consumer confidence and spending later in the financial year.
